items.t: Southampton’s BAT factory remembered for good wages, free food and tobacco haze
sum: Beneath a thick, inescapable haze of blue smoke, an industrial titan once hummed in Southampton, forging fortunes, cementing lifelong friendships, and leaving a scent of tobacco that clung to the city air.
When we recently opened the archives to look back at life inside the British American Tobacco factory, it sparked a phenomenal reaction from those who walked through the Regent's Park Road gates.

Looking back at the golden age of local industry, reader Paul August captured the mood perfectly, remembering: "The good old days when Southampton had a lot of industry/ factory work and people could earn a good wage."
It was an era of robust worker solidarity, too, a stark contrast to the modern economic landscape.
As commenter My Pronouns Common/Sense wryly noted: "LOL! Good old days of when a 6% pay rise resulted in a picket line when inflation was a smidge over 2%."
They pointed out the stark difference in the modern workplace, adding: "Nowadays you're lucky if your pay rise matches the inflation rate."

items.t: British American Tobacco (LSE:BATS) After FDA Velo Nod And JPMorgan Backing Looks Undervalued
sum: Компания British American Tobacco (LSE:BATS) снова оказалась в центре внимания после того, как JPMorgan возобновил освещение с рейтингом «Выше веса», вскоре после того, как FDA разрешило продажу в США 24 никотиновых пакетиков Velo.

В последнее время набирает силу: цена акций British American Tobacco обеспечила доходность в размере 11,15% с начала года и 9,30% за 1 месяц. Совокупная доходность акционеров за 1 год в размере 21,03% сочетается с очень высокой совокупной доходностью акционеров за 5 лет, около 17x.
Загляните за пределы British American Tobacco и сравните ее с тщательно подобранной группой ориентированных на доход акций в наших четырех дивидендных крепостях.

После резкого восстановления и нового оптимизма вокруг никотиновых пакетиков в США настоящая загадка для владельцев British American Tobacco теперь проста. Есть ли значимый потенциал роста еще впереди, или большая его часть уже реализована в ходе недавнего движения?

По сравнению с последним закрытием на уровне 46,56 фунтов стерлингов, согласно консенсусу аналитиков Narrative on Simply Wall St, справедливая стоимость British American Tobacco составляет 51,54 фунтов стерлингов. Это указывает на скромную скидку и закрепляет нынешний отскок в истории с тяжелыми денежными потоками.

Быстрый рост и дальнейшее проникновение современных продуктов для перорального применения и продуктов для подогрева, особенно учитывая, что бездымные продукты уже составляют 19,8% доходов British American Tobacco, а количество потребителей бездымных продуктов достигает 35 миллионов, сохраняет потенциал для продуктов с пониженным риском, которые будут занимать большую долю доходов группы и поддерживать будущий рост выручки.

Активный спрос и премиализация продуктов с пониженным риском, при этом доходы Modern Oral, как ожидается, выиграют от отраслевого пула, который, по прогнозам, к 2030 году вырастет почти втрое и составит примерно 11 миллиардов фунтов стерлингов, а валовая прибыль Modern Oral на единицу продукции, уже указанная примерно в 4 раза, усиливает возможности для структурно более высокой маржинальной прибыли и структуры доходов с течением времени.

British American Tobacco stock gets JPMorgan Overweight call
sum: JPMorgan reinstated coverage of British American Tobacco on November 10, 2026, with an Overweight rating and a 5,300-pence price target. The bank cited the tobacco group's multi-category next-generation product portfolio and its gains in US vapor and nicotine pouches, according to Investing.com.

JPMorgan expects like-for-like growth of 3% to 5% in 2027 as British American Tobacco moves beyond pressure in Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. The bank also pointed to improved recent trends in the US cigarette market as a support for the outlook.

Its central forecast calls for 3.9% like-for-like growth in 2027 and adjusted earnings per share of 389 pence, which is approximately 1% above consensus. JPMorgan set a December 2028 discounted-cash-flow target of 5,300 pence, using a terminal growth rate of negative 0.5% and a weighted average cost of capital of 10.1%.

The investment case rests heavily on the performance of newer nicotine products. JPMorgan said the company's multi-category approach has gained market share in US vapor and nicotine pouches, giving investors a more diversified growth profile beyond traditional combustible tobacco.

The rating follows a similar constructive view from Goldman Sachs, which recently upgraded British American Tobacco to Buy. The two analyst calls put execution in the United States and a recovery across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa at the center of the debate over whether the group can deliver its medium-term growth ambitions.
British American Tobacco stock traded at 54.92 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:50 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

Investor attention now turns to whether British American Tobacco can convert stronger US nicotine-product demand into the projected growth rate while managing regulatory and regional risks. The broader S&P 500 market environment remains a relevant backdrop for global consumer-staples valuations.

British American Tobacco stock gets Goldman growth upgrade
sum: Goldman Sachs upgraded British American Tobacco from Neutral to Buy on Monday, November 2, citing a clearer path toward sustained organic revenue growth, according to a Yahoo Finance report based on Investing.com. The brokerage raised its 12-month price target to 5,600 pence from 5,200 pence.

Goldman expects BAT's organic sales growth to reach about 4% in both 2027 and 2028, moving toward the midpoint of management's 3% to 5% guidance range. The forecast follows four years of low-single-digit growth below that target and rests on resilient combustible tobacco sales and accelerating New Categories such as nicotine pouches and vapour products.

Execution in the United States is central to the thesis. The market accounts for more than 60% of BAT's operating profit, while Velo Max reached 44,000 retail outlets in October after its September launch. Goldman expects a further expansion by January 2027 and also cited a 20% rise in Vuse vapour volumes through August in US states with observable enforcement.

The brokerage expects the Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa region to return to growth from 2027 as headwinds in Bangladesh and Australia ease on a comparative basis. It forecasts medium-term operating profit growth of 5% to 6%, average earnings-per-share growth of 9% over five years and annual free cash flow of about 9.5 billion pounds through 2030, above BAT's guidance of about 8 billion pounds.

The more positive rating does not remove execution risks. Goldman cut its earnings-per-share forecasts for 2027 and 2028 by 0.4% and 1.3%, respectively, citing updated industry assumptions and exchange-rate movements. Regulation, US Food and Drug Administration enforcement and delays in authorizing New Categories remain potential obstacles.

Goldman expects BAT's full-year 2026 trading update in December to show stronger second-half momentum. That release should give investors a fresh measure of New Categories adoption, regional performance and progress toward the group's organic growth target.
British American Tobacco stock traded at 54.32 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:42 CET on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

Russia: Japan Tobacco pays the price for staying
sum: - A decree dated November 5, 2026 hands Japan Tobacco International’s (JTI) four Russian factories to a Russian company, Promyshlennye Aktivy.
- It is the first time Moscow has applied its “temporary management” mechanism to a tobacco company.
- Imperial Brands (2022) and BAT (2023) sold their Russian businesses after the invasion of Ukraine. JTI and Philip Morris stayed.
- Danone, Carlsberg, Nestlé and Auchan have met the same fate. Danone and Carlsberg eventually sold their subsidiaries at a steep discount.

Decree No. 817, signed on November 5, adds JTI’s stakes in four Russian companies to the list of assets under temporary management: Petro and JTI Donskoy Tabak, which make cigarettes in St. Petersburg and Rostov-on-Don, and JTI Yelets and Kres Neva, which process raw tobacco. The sites employ around 4,000 people. The largest, Petro, posted a record net profit of 13.2 billion rubles in 2023.

The decree gives no reason for the move. Nor does it say who the new manager is. Several Russian companies go by the name Promyshlennye Aktivy (which simply means “industrial assets”), and the decree provides no identifier showing which one is taking charge. According to independent Russian media, one of them may be linked to Taimuraz Bolloev, a long-time associate of Vladimir Putin. The name is a familiar one: Bolloev is the man Moscow installed at the head of the Baltika brewery after it seized Carlsberg’s business in 2023.

On paper, JTI remains the owner. The Kremlin insists these decrees are not aimed at changing ownership. But temporary management has no end date, and it is the managers appointed by Moscow who call the shots.

BAT Shareholders Digest a Busy Week: Capital Group Stake Slips, Goldman Turns Buyer, Organigram Bet
sum: British American Tobacco packed a remarkable amount of corporate news into the first week of November, and the market's verdict on Friday was unkind — though not for any reason the company itself disclosed. The FTSE 100 heavyweight shed 2.5% as a broad flight from risk swept London equities, with Reuters linking the selloff to mounting anxiety over artificial intelligence. BAT closed the session at 54.84 €, and press coverage counted it among the leading fallers on the UK benchmark index.

Media commentary pointed to worries about declining volumes in traditional tobacco products, regulatory pressure and a rotation out of defensive consumer names as drags on the stock, with BAT faring worse than its own sector. Those explanations come from market reporting rather than from any company-confirmed trigger.

The same Friday brought a regulatory disclosure showing The Capital Group Companies had trimmed its voting stake in the cigarette maker. Its holding slipped from 18.023677% to 17.975584%, with the relevant threshold crossed on Wednesday. The mandatory filing puts Capital Group's reported position at roughly 387 million voting rights.

Sentiment had received a more supportive nudge earlier in the week. On 2 November, according to media reports, Goldman Sachs upgraded BAT from "Neutral" to "Buy" and raised its twelve-month price target from 5,200 to 5,600 pence — changing both its recommendation and its valuation mark for the shares.

The buyback programme also generated paperwork. BAT reported on 2 November the repurchase of about 597,000 ordinary shares, bought between 26 and 30 October with the intention of cancelling them. On Tuesday the company corrected its 2 November disclosure of own-account transactions: Merrill Lynch International, not Goldman Sachs International, was named as the counterparty. All other details stood unchanged.

Further afield, Organigram Global said on 3 November that BAT, through subsidiary BT DE Investments Inc., had agreed a £100 million investment connected to Organigram's proposed acquisition of Aurora Cannabis. The tobacco group is to subscribe for 141 million Organigram shares at C$1.33 apiece. Completion is expected in January 2027, subject to the necessary approvals.

BAT Slides With London Market as Boardroom Changes and a Goldman Upgrade Draw Focus
sum: British American Tobacco shares shed 2.5% on Friday, caught in a broad global equities selloff that Reuters linked to investor anxiety over artificial intelligence. The news agency counted the cigarette maker among the London heavyweights dragging the FTSE 100 lower, with the stock closing the session at €54.84. Media reports also placed the London tobacco sector among the weakest industries in the FTSE 350 as the wider UK market finished in the red.

Against that soft backdrop, corporate news flow around the company stayed busy. Goldman Sachs lifted its rating on BAT from Neutral to Buy on Monday, raising its 12-month price target to £56 from £52. The analysts pointed to a clearer route toward sustained organic revenue growth, framing the upgrade and the higher target as two parts of a single reassessment.

Directors were buying shares in the meantime. Seven senior executives, including CEO Tadeu Marroco and COO Johan Vandermeulen, each acquired three ordinary shares through the company's Partnership Share Scheme on Wednesday, according to a regulatory disclosure published Thursday. The purchase price came to £45.325 per share, with all seven executives reporting the same transaction size and the same dealing day.

BAT also disclosed a C$187.5 million investment in Organigram on Tuesday. Structured as a private placement, the funding is intended to help Organigram finance its acquisition of Aurora Cannabis, with Organigram acting as buyer and Aurora as the target.

On the governance front, the company announced on 28 October that Bruce Sewell would join the board as an independent non-executive director, effective 1 January 2027. Sewell is also slated to serve on the audit and nomination committees. Separate changes to the composition of the company's committees are set to take effect on 30 November 2026.
Finally, The Capital Group Companies reported a reduction in its voting rights in British American Tobacco, from 18.023677% to 17.975584%.

BAT's C$187.5 Million Organigram Bet Lands Alongside FDA Nod for Velo and a Goldman Upgrade
sum: British American Tobacco has committed C$187.5 million to buy Organigram shares at C$1.33 apiece, a capital pledge tied to Organigram's takeover of Aurora Cannabis and timed to close alongside that deal. Organigram, not BAT, is the acquirer of Aurora. Press reports suggested the funding commitment helped finance the transaction, and coverage linked BAT's share-price slide on Tuesday to the investment agreement — though the company's own disclosures do not establish that connection.

The stock's retreat continued into a second session, with shares down 2.3% as a global selloff in technology stocks weighed on London markets. Media reports described a weaker open for the London exchange, with losses also hitting the FTSE 100 and AstraZeneca.

Regulatory news offered a counterweight. On 30 October the US Food and Drug Administration authorised the marketing of 24 Velo nicotine pouch products, each containing 4 mg of nicotine. The manufacturer is Modoral Brands, an operating company of Reynolds American within the BAT group.

On the capital-return side, BAT reported on Monday the repurchase of 596,824 of its own ordinary shares under its buyback programme, with the purchases made between 26 and 30 October. The company separately disclosed the issuance and allotment of 45,205 ordinary shares under its Sharesave employee savings plan between 1 and 30 October.

Goldman Sachs lifted its rating on BAT from "Neutral" to "Buy" on Monday, according to media reports, and raised its price target to 5,600 pence from 5,200 pence. The analysts pointed to a clearer path toward sustainable organic revenue growth.

Governance changes are also in motion. BAT announced on 28 October the appointment of Bruce Sewell as an independent non-executive director, effective 1 January 2027. He will also serve on the audit and nomination committees.

Filings showed a reduced voting stake held by The Capital Group Companies at 17.975584%, down from 18.023677%, with the relevant threshold crossed on Wednesday. The shares fell 2.5% that day; the disclosure does not establish a link between the price move and the stake notice.

British American Tobacco stock faces weak BAT Bangladesh earnings
sum: British American Tobacco stock traded at 55.89 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:41 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026. The latest regional earnings signal came from BAT Bangladesh PLC, which reported a sharp decline in third-quarter profit.

According to The Business Standard, BAT Bangladesh reported the figures for the quarter ended September 30 on October 29. Net profit after tax fell 67.28% year on year to 99.84 crore taka from 305.04 crore taka in the same quarter of 2025.

Quarterly earnings per share declined to 1.85 taka from 5.65 taka. Net revenue from contracts with customers fell to 1,259 crore taka from 1,677.13 crore taka a year earlier. The report attributed the weaker result to lower revenue and higher operating expenses.

The deterioration extended across the first nine months of 2026. BAT Bangladesh said net profit after tax fell 28.77% to 513.02 crore taka from 720.26 crore taka in the same period of 2025. Nine-month net revenue declined to 5,090 crore taka from 5,754 crore taka, while earnings per share fell to 9.50 taka from 13.34 taka.

The company reported gross revenue of 7,328.34 crore taka for the quarter. Supplementary duty and value-added tax deductions amounted to 6,068.78 crore taka, highlighting the importance of tax and pricing conditions in the local tobacco market.

The Bangladesh figures concern a locally listed company and are not consolidated results for British American Tobacco plc. They nevertheless provide a regional operating signal for investors monitoring tobacco demand, taxation and cost pressure in South Asian markets. The reported contraction also shows how quickly local earnings can diverge from broader group expectations.

For the parent company's shares, the immediate focus remains on group-level revenue growth, new nicotine categories and capital allocation. The Bangladesh report alone does not establish a change in British American Tobacco plc's consolidated outlook or explain the movement of its stock.

Organigram-Aurora $561 million deal taps Goodmans, Torys, Stikeman Elliott, Paul Weiss
sum: Canadian cannabis deal brings together four law firms as Organigram seeks to acquire Aurora at 93% premium

Organigram Global Inc. has engaged Goodmans LLP as its legal adviser for its proposed C$561 million acquisition of Aurora Cannabis Inc., which is advised by Stikeman Elliott LLP and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP. Torys LLP is advising Aurora’s special committee, while Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt LLP is acting as legal counsel to British American Tobacco, Organigram’s strategic shareholder.

BMO Capital Markets is serving as Organigram’s financial adviser and has provided a fairness opinion to its investment committee and board. Fort Capital Partners is advising Aurora and has provided a fairness opinion, while Origin Merchant Partners is advising Aurora’s special committee and has also provided a fairness opinion.

The proposed acquisition emerged from a strategic review undertaken by Aurora under the oversight of its independent directors’ special committee, following Curaleaf’s unsolicited takeover proposal. The committee and Aurora’s board have unanimously recommended the Organigram transaction to shareholders, describing it as the best actionable route to maximise shareholder value.

Under the arrangement agreement, Aurora shareholders can elect to receive C$7.80 in cash, 5.8626 Organigram shares, or a combination of C$3.75 in cash and 3.0431 Organigram shares for each Aurora share, subject to proration limits.
Aurora shareholders are expected to hold approximately 35% of the combined company’s economic ownership on a fully diluted basis and 42% of its voting ownership.

The combined entity aims to strengthen its position in Canada, Europe and Australia by bringing together Organigram’s recreational cannabis business and research and development capabilities with Aurora’s international medical cannabis operations and EU-GMP-certified manufacturing facilities.

Aurora Cannabis Stock Surges on Organigram Deal
sum: Aurora Cannabis Inc ACB shares are booming Tuesday after the company agreed to be acquired by Organigram Global for 7.80 Canadian dollars ($5.57) per share, a deal that tops a rival hostile offer from Curaleaf. Here’s what you should know.
- Aurora Cannabis stock is surging to new heights today. Why is ACB stock up today?

Aurora Cannabis shares are rising after Organigram agreed to buy the company for C$7.80 a share, an equity value of about C$561 million. Aurora holders pick how they get paid. They can take all cash, take only Organigram stock at 5.8626 shares for each of their own, or split the payment between C$3.75 in cash and 3.0431 Organigram shares.

The price is 93% above Aurora’s price on Aug. 10, the final complete session before Curaleaf revealed its hostile plan, and 21% above Curaleaf’s current bid, which was last amended on Oct. 6. Aurora’s board unanimously rejected that bid. It now calls the Organigram deal better for shareholders and tells them not to tender to Curaleaf.

The two Canadian cannabis companies say they would run five sites with EU-GMP certification and hold leadership positions in Canada, Europe and Australia. They also count on more than C$50 million in synergies. After closing, Aurora holders would own about 35% of the combined economics and hold 42% of the votes. Organigram CEO James Yamanaka called the deal a “defining step” for the company’s strategy.
British American Tobacco, Organigram’s cornerstone shareholder, will buy about C$187.5 million of new Organigram shares at C$1.33 to help pay the cash portion.

Two-thirds of the votes cast by Aurora shareholders must back the deal, and so must a majority of the holders outside certain insiders. Organigram shareholders also vote, and British American Tobacco’s 30% of Organigram’s votes is committed in favor even though it sits outside that count.

British American Tobacco stock faces dividend date as 2026 outlook holds
sum: British American Tobacco is heading into a scheduled dividend payment while keeping its 2026 revenue outlook unchanged. Simply Wall St reports that eligible shareholders are due to receive 0.6126 pounds per share on Friday, November 6, after an October 1 ex-dividend date and an October 2 record date.

The payment is part of BAT's quarterly distribution plan. The company declared a total interim dividend of 2.4504 pounds per ordinary share for the year ending December 31, 2026, with equal instalments scheduled across May, August, November and February, according to the dividend information carried by Simply Wall St.

BAT continues to target 2026 revenue growth of 3% to 5% at constant exchange rates, adjusted for Canada. The company expects performance toward the lower end of that range. The guidance was reaffirmed in the company's 2026 updates, including the half-year report listed on BAT's press release page.

The outlook reflects a business still balancing resilient combustible tobacco operations with investment in newer nicotine categories. BAT's half-year materials described performance as in line with expectations, while the company has continued to emphasize growth in vapour, heated products and modern oral products such as nicotine pouches.

That mix is important for investors because the long-term growth case depends increasingly on products outside traditional cigarettes. At its September Capital Markets Day, BAT set out ambitions for its Horizon 2030 strategy, while maintaining its medium-term growth algorithm. Execution in New Categories, pricing, currency movements and the pace of cigarette-volume declines remain key variables for earnings and cash generation.

British American Tobacco stock traded at 55.43 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 09:20 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 0.56 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. Investors can follow the real-time quote of British American Tobacco stock.
The scheduled distribution provides a near-term cash-return event, but the central valuation question remains whether New Category growth can offset pressure on the legacy portfolio.

BTI vs. PM: Which Tobacco Dividend Will Actually Survive the Industry’s Decline?
sum: Both BTI and PM fund generous dividends from a shrinking cigarette business, but one company's smoke-free pivot has already changed what its payout is built on, and that gap matters far more than the headline yield difference.

British American Tobacco (NYSE:BTI | BTI Price Prediction) or Philip Morris International (NYSE:PM): which Big Tobacco dividend should an investor planning for retirement own right now? Both fund their payouts from cigarettes in structural decline, and both are spending heavily to replace them with smoke-free products. The better pick is the company whose transition already pays the bills. On that test, Philip Morris wins, even though BAT carries the higher headline yield and cheaper valuation.

The market agrees. Philip Morris shares are up 21.91% year to date, while BAT is down 0.71%. Over 10 years on an adjusted basis, Philip Morris gained 221.75% against 67.32% for BAT. Morningstar noted today that BAT’s Capital Markets Day reaffirmed its midterm growth algorithm, but the market expects far worse.

Philip Morris just lifted its quarterly dividend from $1.47 to $1.60, payable October 26, 2026, for an annualized forward rate of $6.40. That follows an 8.9% increase in 2025, and its record shows steady quarterly payments stretching back to June 2008. The trailing yield is 3.03%.

BAT declared 245.04p per share for FY2025, paid in four payments of 61.26p, a 2.0% raise. Structure matters here. BAT is a UK-based foreign private issuer whose U.S. shares trade as American depositary receipts, and it commits to dividend growth in sterling terms. The dollar check a U.S. holder receives therefore moves with the exchange rate: the quarterly payment was $0.746191 in 2021, dipped to $0.700605 in 2023 and now stands at $0.834851. Philip Morris, a U.S.-domiciled corporation, declares and pays in dollars. Winner: Philip Morris.

Philip Morris expects roughly $13.5 billion of operating cash flow in 2026, and Q2 operating cash flow rose 61% to $5.492 billion. Raised 2026 guidance calls for adjusted diluted EPS of $8.26 to $8.41, well above the $6.40 annualized dividend.

Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Philip Morris, British American Tobacco and Altria Group
sum: Chicago, IL – June 22, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research Philip Morris International Inc. PM, British American Tobacco p.l.c. BTI and Altria Group, Inc. MO
Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/2939153/3-tobacco-stocks-to-keep-an-eye-on-amid-market-headwinds

The Zacks Tobacco industry is navigating a challenging operating environment marked by persistent pressure on cigarette volumes, elevated costs and a rapidly evolving product landscape. Inflationary and macroeconomic pressures, changing consumer preferences and regulatory restrictions on tobacco sales and marketing continue to weigh on traditional cigarette consumption. Meanwhile, higher costs for key inputs such as tobacco leaf, energy and labor, along with increased investments in next-generation products, are creating additional pressure on margins.

Despite these headwinds, leading players such as Philip Morris International Inc., British American Tobacco p.l.c. and Altria Group, Inc. are demonstrating resilience through their focus on smoke-free alternatives. By expanding across heated tobacco, vapor and oral nicotine categories, these companies are aligning with shifting consumer preferences and positioning for long-term growth in an evolving landscape.

The Zacks Tobacco industry includes companies that manufacture and sell cigarettes as well as tobacco and nicotine-based products, such as cigars, snuffs and oral tobacco. Some companies also offer reduced-risk products (RRPs), such as e-cigarettes, vaping and heat-not-burn variants.

A few of the firms are engaged in making devices and attachments needed in vaping and heat-not-burn products. Most products manufactured by the tobacco industry participants fall under the strict vigilance of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and are required to follow the permissible levels of nicotine in manufacturing.

Players in this space sell products mostly through large retailers, distributors, convenience stores, drugstores, wholesalers and grocery chains. Some international tobacco firms also operate in the country through subsidiaries.

Philip Morris: Why Numbers Point to a $240 Share Price
sum: Philip Morris (PM), the global tobacco and nicotine giant executing one of consumer staples’ most credible smoke-free transformations, crossed a structural milestone in 2025 as smoke-free products generated $17 billion in revenue, now 41.5% of total net revenues, with shares trading near $176.

The February 6 Q4 earnings call confirmed the trigger: adjusted diluted EPS of $7.54 for full-year 2025, up 15% in dollar terms and the strongest growth since 2011, while ZYN, PMI’s oral nicotine pouch brand that competes directly in the fastest-growing U.S. nicotine segment, shipped 794 million cans, up 37%.

ZYN held 61.5% U.S. can volume share and over 67% value share even as rival Velo, British American Tobacco’s competing pouch brand, claimed the number-two position, underscoring that category leadership is widening in dollar terms faster than unit terms.

Just today, Philip Morris announced a $50 million, 10-year investment in a Tampa Business Solutions Center expected to create 180 jobs across finance, data engineering, and technology, a concrete operational commitment that signals the infrastructure buildout supporting the company’s accelerating U.S. smoke-free expansion.

Furthermore, CFO Emmanuel Babeau stated on the Q4 2025 earnings call that “we’ve been passing 40% OI margin,” and management targets $45 billion in aggregate operating cash flow through 2028 alongside a leverage ratio approaching 2x, as pending FDA action on ZYN Ultra, a higher-strength pouch product, and a potential IQOS ILUMA U.S. launch position PMI for a second leg of domestic smoke-free growth.

PMI’s smoke-free mix shift, which drove smoke-free products to 41.5% of revenues in 2025, directly supports TIKR’s projection of $8.44 normalized EPS in 2026, up 11.9% from $7.54, as higher-margin ZYN pouches and IQOS heat-not-burn devices displace lower-margin cigarette volume.

TIKR estimates revenue reaching $43.7 billion in 2026 and $46.7 billion in 2027, backed by PMI’s own guidance of 5%–7% organic net revenue growth and a smoke-free portfolio generating 2.5x more gross profit per unit than combustibles.

BAT Malaysia MD Nedal Salem to step down on Aug 1, Daniel Hsu to take over
sum: KUALA LUMPUR (March 5): British American Tobacco (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:BAT) announced on Thursday that its managing director Nedal Salem will be concluding his tenure on Aug 1 after leading the company for four and a half years.
Nedal, 56, will be succeeded by Daniel Hsu, current general manager of BAT Vietnam Cluster, according to a company statement.

"Nedal was instrumental in steering BAT Malaysia through a complex operating environment, which included Malaysia’s first excise hike in over a decade and the implementation of the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 (Act 852).
"Under his stewardship, the group strengthened its commercial resilience, operational discipline and reinforced its combustible portfolio," said BAT Malaysia.

The company said Hsu, 51, brings more than two decades of experience spanning general management, brand marketing, sales, mergers and acquisitions, and joint-venture leadership across multiple industries and markets.

Prior to this appointment, he served as Vietnam cluster general manager at BAT Vietnam, a role he has held since 2021. He previously held leadership roles including cluster general manager for Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau, as well as general manager in Cambodia.
BAT Malaysia’s share price closed up 13 sen or 2.08% at RM6.38, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM1.82 billion.

This announcement was coupled with a reported loss for the fourth quarter of 2025 and a substantial decline in earnings per share for the full year 2025. The subsidiary attributed these financial setbacks to lower turnover, increased operating costs, and a one-off negative impact stemming from a factory relocation and restructuring efforts. Such a sharp deterioration in a subsidiary's financial performance, particularly concerning dividends and profitability, can trigger broader investor concerns about the parent company's overall financial health and its ability to sustain its own dividend payouts, which are often a key attraction for tobacco investors.

While the company had previously updated its fiscal year 2026 earnings guidance in February, providing revenue figures that were below consensus estimates, this earlier guidance did not immediately cause a similar sharp decline, suggesting the subsidiary's news is the more immediate catalyst. Ongoing discussions surrounding U.S. vaping regulations also remain a background factor for investor sentiment, contributing to general market caution for the tobacco sector. items.t: BAT Malaysia’s 4Q profit surges on cigarette retail price hike, higher shipments
sum: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 9): British American Tobacco (M) Bhd (KL:BAT) closed its latest fiscal year with its strongest quarter in seven years on the back of the retail price hike of its cigarette brands and higher shipment volumes.

Net profit for the fourth quarter ended Dec 31, 2025 (4QFY2025) more than doubled to RM121.2 million from RM48.97 million a year earlier, according to a bourse filing on Monday. Revenue rose 45.2% to RM947.98 million from RM653.03 million.

Retail prices of BAT Malaysia's cigarette brands, which include Dunhill, Benson & Hedges, Peter Stuyvesant, KYO, Rothmans and Luckies, were hiked in November last year following the two-sen-per-stick excise duty hike announced under Budget 2026.
The group said volume surged 172% as retailers built up stock ahead of the retail price adjustment. This, combined with cost optimisation initiatives, contributed to the strong earnings, it added.
BAT Malaysia declared a fourth interim dividend of 39 sen per share, amounting to RM111.36 million, to be paid on April 10, bringing full-year payout to 63.5 sen per share.
For the full financial year, BAT Malaysia's net profit was up 10.5% to RM202.45 million from RM183.14 million in FY2024, as revenue slipped 5.2% to RM2.20 billion from RM2.32 billion.
The group's performance in the final quarter amounted to over half of full-year earnings.
